question: Can a stale proposal carrying {repository_node_id,generation,effect_id} be rejected after repository delete/recreate or rollback by a Chat-native authoritative sink that needs no protected/admin setup, richer-mode/manual execution, external hosted coordination, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental monetary cost?

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents per-file update preconditioning with the blob sha of the file being replaced and a 409 Conflict response; this is current-file CAS, not a documented monotonic generation floor outside repository rollback state.

GitHub documents node_id/id as a global identifier for objects addressable across REST/GraphQL. In the inspected page, no monotonic freshness ordering or rollback-independent minimum-generation guarantee is specified.

constructed_model.scope: 13 deterministic histories over authoritative generation g2, proposal node/generation identity, repository-visible node/generation and repository effect marker, sink minimum-generation floor, and sink effect-id history. No destructive repository action was executed.
constructed_model.safety_rule: Apply only when proposal generation is the true current generation and effect_id has not already been authoritatively applied.

mechanisms.repository_only_current_identity_and_eff: Require proposal node/generation to equal repository-visible current node/generation and require repository-local effect marker absent.
mechanisms.co_rollback_sink_floor_strict: Additionally require a sink-local floor to exist, proposal generation >= that floor, and sink-local effect_id absent; floor/effect history are allowed to roll back or disappear with the same failure domain.
mechanisms.ideal_rollback_independent_sink_floor_pl: Atomically require proposal generation >= rollback-independent durable minimum equal to the true authoritative generation and effect_id not already consumed, while retaining the repository current-identity check. This is an abstract capability test, not an identified deployable Chat-native mechanism.

co_rollback_sink_floor_strict.interpretation: Failing closed on a missing floor blocks one valid current proposal, but a floor that itself rolls back below the true generation still admits stale authority; loss of sink effect-id history still admits duplicate retry.

ideal_rollback_independent_sink_floor_pl.interpretation: Within this finite model, both a rollback-independent monotonic generation floor and rollback-independent single-use effect identity are sufficient together. Either property alone is insufficient for both stale-authority and ambiguous-retry safety.

new_evidence.positive_mechanism_property: A sink-side atomic guard {generation >= durable_min_generation AND effect_id not previously consumed} is sufficient in the tested histories even when repository-visible identity and repository-local markers are rolled back.
new_evidence.falsification: Repository-only current-node/generation CAS is not rollback-independent: after the repository-visible state rolls back to the stale proposal's node/generation, the stale proposal becomes observationally current again. A sink floor co-located in the same rollback domain reduces failures but does not solve floor rollback or lost idempotency history.
new_evidence.availability_result: No accepted concrete Chat-native authoritative sink was identified in this bounded leaf. The inspected GitHub repository primitives provide current-object identity and per-file CAS, but this leaf found no documented rollback-domain-independent monotonic floor plus durable single-use effect-id gate that is usable without protected/admin setup or external hosted coordination.

observation_vs_inference.observed: Official GitHub documentation exposes per-file sha preconditioning/409 conflict and global object node IDs.
observation_vs_inference.inferred_from_constructed_histories: Any authority state that can co-rollback to the stale world's state cannot distinguish that history from a world in which the stale generation was never superseded; therefore it cannot by itself prove freshness after full co-rollback.
observation_vs_inference.not_claimed: No claim is made that GitHub repository deletion/restoration necessarily reuses or changes a particular node_id, or that every possible Chat connector lacks a suitable sink capability. The negative availability claim is limited to the role-permitted mechanism surfaces inspected in this bounded leaf.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.unresolved_child: Identify or rule out a rollback-domain-independent, role-permitted Chat-native authoritative sink that atomically enforces a monotonic minimum generation and durable single-use effect_id without protected/admin setup, richer-mode/manual execution, external hosted coordination, or finite monthly/trial/paid quota.

scope_guard: Only the two inspected GitHub documentation surfaces and 13 constructed histories. No destructive repository operation, no external sink mutation, and no generalization to arbitrary connectors or undocumented GitHub restore semantics.
continuation: Part102: execute exactly one bounded rollback-independent-sink availability leaf. Inspect only public official documentation for role-permitted GitHub-native candidate surfaces that could hold a monotonic minimum-generation witness outside ordinary repository-content rollback (for example ruleset/protection metadata, append-only object surfaces, or server-enforced immutable identity), and test each against three gates: no protected/admin/manual setup, no finite monthly/trial/paid quota or incremental cost, and atomic rejection of {generation below floor OR repeated effect_id}. If every candidate either shares the rollback domain, is mutable/deletable, lacks atomic generation+effect-id enforcement, or requires protected/admin/external coordination, persist that exact capability gap and select the next non-conflicting claim/idempotency leaf without declaring Phase 1 complete.
